outcome: Stillbirth (fetal death before and during delivery)
Neonatal death (live born with death 0-27 days postpartum)
cohort: The study included 4,590,853 singletons identified through data linkage between nationwide Medical Birth Registries in Denmark (1994-2014), Norway and Sweden (1988-2015), comprising 78,642 conceived by fresh-ET, 18,084 by frozen-ET, and the remainder conceived without medical assistance.
finding: The risk of stillbirth was similar after fresh-ET and frozen-ET compared with singletons conceived without medical assistance, while neonatal mortality was higher after both fresh-ET (OR, 1.69) and frozen-ET (OR, 1.51), possibly mediated by the higher risk of preterm birth in these groups.
gest_age: Measured as preterm birth (<37 gestational weeks) and specific gestational week categories (22-27 weeks)
